To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
fusion of CT, MR, and SPECT images of hemangiomas is feasible, accurate, and useful for the diagnosis and management of these lesions.

we have developed a method of image analysis that can be used to correlate hepatic hemangioma detected at CT and/or MR imaging with increased blood-pool activity evident at Tc-99M-labeled red blood cells SPECT.

(1) fusion of MR, Tc-99M SPECT, and CT images of the liver can be performed with high precision and (2) this technique can be used to confirm the presence of small hepatic hemangioma with high sensitivity and specificity.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of an image analysis method that enables correlation of hemangioma detected at MR, CT, or both with increased blood pool activities evident at Tc-99M-labeled RBC SPECT.
the development of an image analysis technique that allows for accurate registration of MR and CT images with SPECT images.
the development and evaluation of image fusion algorithms for the analysis of SPECT and CT or MR images of the liver.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
fusion of SPECT images of Tc-99-labeled red blood cells with CT and MR images is a powerful tool for the diagnosis and characterization of hepatic hemangioma.
the fusion of CT and MR images with SPECT images of Tc-99 red blood cell uptake in the liver provides a useful tool for diagnosis and evaluation of hepatic hemangioma.
the technique of image registration and fusion is a useful adjunct in the diagnostic evaluation of patients with suspected hepatic hemangioma.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the fusion of MR, Tc-99 red blood cell SCEPT and CT images provides a powerful diagnostic tool in the detection of hepatic hemangioma.
the fusion of SPECT with CT or MR images provides a powerful diagnostic tool for the evaluation of hepatic hemangioma.
the method of image analysis described herein provides a reliable means of correlation of hemangioma activity seen at SPECT with lesions detected at CT and MR.
The main takeaway from our work is that

fusion of CT, MR, and SPECT images provides an accurate method for confirming the presence of hemangiomas and can be used for evaluation of lesions located adjacent to large intrahepatic blood vessels.
image registration is a powerful tool for the fusion of different imaging modalities.
image fusion is a useful tool for the diagnostic workup of hemangiomas, especially in the case of small lesions.
